h: Noach, Adam, and Three Mitzvot of Repair
The mitzvot of women and the Torah’s spiritual archetypes reveal a path to repair the sin of Adam.
Challah, Niddah, and Shabbat Candle Lighting

p: בְּתַנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ פָּתַח:
— In Midrash Tanchuma at the beginning of this parashah it opens:
יְלַמְּדֵנוּ רַבֵּינוּ, עַל כַּמָּה עֲבֵירוֹת נָשִׁים מֵתוֹת וְכוּלֵי,
— ‘Let our master teach us: for how many transgressions do women die, etc.?’
עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה וְכוּלֵי, וּשְׁלָשְׁתָּן מִן הַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי;
— For three, etc., and all three are from the Torah, etc.;
וּלְהָבִין שַׁיָּיכוּת פְּתִיחָה זוֹ לְפָרָשָׁה זוֹ.
— and one must understand the connection of this opening discourse to this parashah.
וְהִנֵּה בַּמִּשְׁנָה נִשְׁנֵית בְּמַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת (לא:),
— Now behold, in the Mishnah this is taught in tractate Shabbat (31b),
וּמִסְּתָמָא יֵשׁ לִשְׁלָשְׁתָּן שַׁיָּיכוּת לְמַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת,
— and presumably all three have intrinsic relevance to tractate Shabbat,
אַף דְּחַלָּה וְנִדָּה נוֹהֵג תָּמִיד.
— even though the mitzvot of challah and niddah apply constantly.
אָכֵן הָעִנְיָן, דְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר:
— Indeed, the matter is as stated in the Midrash:
"שָׁפְכָה דָּמוֹ וְכוּלֵי – תִּשְׁפּוֹךְ דָּמָהּ וְתִשְׁמוֹר נִדָּתָהּ וְכוּלֵי;
— ‘She spilled his blood, etc.—let her shed her blood and observe her niddah, etc.;
הִיא טִמְּאָה חַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי;
— she defiled the challah of the world, etc.;
הִיא כִּבְּתָה נֵרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם וְכוּלֵי"
— she extinguished the candle of man, etc.’—
שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים שֶׁחָשַׁב הֵם כְּנֶגֶד הַגּוּף, וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְהַנְּשָׁמָה:
— these three things that he enumerated correspond to the body, the nefesh, and the neshamah:
"טִמְּאָה חַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם" נֶגֶד הַגּוּף,
— ‘She defiled the challah of the world’ corresponds to the physical body,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה מְקַשְׁקֶשֶׁת עִיסָּתָהּ בְּמַיִם וְכוּלֵי,
— and as is stated: just as a woman mixes her dough with water, etc.,
כָּךְ עָשָׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן וְכוּלֵי:
— so the Holy One, blessed be He, did with Adam the First, etc.:
"וַיִּיצֶר ה' אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם עָפָר וְגוֹמֵר",
— ‘And Hashem God formed man of the dust, etc.’,
וְזֶה קָאֵי עַל גּוּף שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהוּא חַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם.
— and this refers to the body of Adam the First, who is the challah-offering of the world.
וְאָמַר "טִמְּאָה חַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם"
— And it said ‘she defiled the challah of the world’
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קמו עַמּוּד א):
— based on what they said (Shabbat 146a):
שֶׁבָּא נָחָשׁ עַל חַוָּה הֵטִיל בָּהּ זוּהֲמָא;
— when the Serpent came upon Eve he injected contamination into her;
יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָתָן וְכוּלֵי,
— Israel who stood at Mount Sinai, their contamination ceased, etc.,
וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כַּהֲנָא וְכוּלֵי:
— and this disputes the view of Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, etc.:
עַד שְׁלֹשָׁה דוֹרוֹת לֹא פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ וְכוּלֵי.
— until three generations contamination did not cease from our Forefathers, etc.
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ דְּ"אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים",
— And we have already explained that ‘both these and those are the words of the living God’,
שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִצִּדּוֹ כְּבָר פָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא מִמֶּנּוּ,
— for Jacob our father, peace be upon him, from his own personal perspective contamination had already ceased from him,
שֶׁהָיָה כְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל.
— for he was like Adam the First prior to the corrupting sin.
וְאָמַר מַה שֶּׁקַּל שֶׁבַּקַּלִּים אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר כֵּן,
— And he said that which the lightest of the light does not say,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י וַיֵּצֵא מִבְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה),
— as stated (in Rashi's commentary, Vayeitzei, from Bereishit Rabbah),
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הִרְגִּישׁ כְּלָל הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף
— because he felt no bodily physical pleasure whatsoever
וְלֹא יָדַע בּוּשָׁה בָּזֶה,
— and felt no shame in this,
כְּמוֹ בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל דִּכְתִיב: "וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ",
— just as with Adam the First prior to the fall, concerning whom it is written: ‘and they were not ashamed’,
וְהוֹלִיד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָּהֶן דֹּפִי.
— and he fathered twelve tribes in whom there was no blemish.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לֹא הָיָה עוֹד שֶׁפָּסְקָה זוּהֲמָא מִכָּל זַרְעוֹ
— Nevertheless, in outward manifestation it was not yet the case that contamination ceased from all his seed
עַד שֶׁעָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי,
— until they stood at Mount Sinai,
דִּכְתִיב: "אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם".
— as it is written: ‘I said: You are godlike beings’.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁהִיא "טִמְּאָה חַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם",
— And this is what it meant that she ‘defiled the challah of the world’,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֵטִיל הַנָּחָשׁ בָּהּ הַזּוּהֲמָא
— in that because the Serpent injected contamination into her,
פָּשְׁטָה הַזּוּהֲמָא בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן וּבְזַרְעוֹ עַד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— the contamination spread through Adam the First and through his seed until Jacob our father, peace be upon him,
וּבְזַרְעוֹ עַד מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
— and through his seed until the Giving of the Torah;
אַךְ עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ יֵצֶר הָרָע.
— yet even so there still remains the evil inclination.
"וְשָׁפְכָה אֶת דָּמוֹ" כְּנֶגֶד הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
— ‘And she spilled his blood’ corresponds to the nefesh,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי הַדָּם הוּא הַנָּפֶשׁ".
— and as is stated: ‘for the blood is the nefesh’.
"הִיא כִּבְּתָה נֵרוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם" הוּא נֶגֶד הַנְּשָׁמָה,
— ‘She extinguished the candle of the world’ corresponds to the neshamah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּמִּדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא דִּכְתִיב: "נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם".
— and as stated in Midrash Tanchuma, for it is written: ‘The spirit of man is the lamp of Hashem’.
וְשַׁבָּת הוּא הַזְּמַן לְתַקֵּן כָּל קִלְקוּל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— And Shabbat is the appointed time to rectify the entire corruption of Adam the First,
שֶׁתְּחִלַּת פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה בַּאֲכִילָה,
— for the initial blemish of the Serpent occurred through eating,
וַאֲכִילָה דְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא בִּקְדוּשָׁה בָּא לְתַקֵּן זֶה,
— and the eating of Shabbat, being in holiness, comes to rectify this,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח.):
— and as is stated (Sanhedrin 38a):
אָדָם נִבְרָא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי
— Adam was created on the eve of Shabbat, etc.,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס לִסְעוּדָה מִיָּד;
— so that he should enter directly into the banquet;
וּבְאָבוֹת דְּרַבִּי נָתָן (פֶּרֶק א) הַגִּרְסָא:
— and in Avot DeRabbi Natan (chapter 1) the textual variant is:
"שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס לִסְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת מִיָּד",
— ‘that he should enter into the Sabbath meal immediately’,
וְהַיְינוּ כְּדֵי לְתַקֵּן הַקִּלְקוּל,
— which means precisely in order to rectify the corruption;
וְזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת מִשְׁנָה זוֹ לְמַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת.
— and this is the deep connection of this Mishnah to tractate Shabbat.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 146a:1: “the snake came upon Eve, i.e., when it seduced her to eat from the Tree of Knowledge, it infected her with moral contamination, and this contamination remained in all human beings. When the Jewish people stood at Mount Sinai, their contamination ceased, whereas gentiles did not stand at Mount Sinai, and their contamination never ceased. Rav Aḥa, the son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi: What about converts? How do you explain the cessation of their moral contamination? Rav Ashi said to him: Even though they themselves were not at Mount Sinai, their guardian angels were present, as it is written: “It is not with you alone that I make this covenant and this oath, but with he that stands here with us today before the Lord our God, and with he that is not here with us today” (Deuteronomy 29:13–14), and this includes converts.”

paragraphs.text: Avot DeRabbi Natan 1:8: “R. Judah b. Bathyra said: Adam, the first man, was reclining in the Garden of Eden with ministering angels at his service, roasting meat and cooling wine for him. Then the serpent came and, seeing him in all his glory, at once grew envious of him. How was Adam, the first man, created? In the first hour his dust was gathered together, in the second his outline was shaped, in the third he was made into solid substance, in the fourth his limbs were articulated, in the fifth his orifices were opened, in the sixth a soul was infused into him, in the seventh he stood on his feet, in the eighth Eve became his mate, in the ninth he was brought into the Garden of Eden, in the tenth he received his command [concerning the tree], in the eleventh he sinned, and in the twelfth he was driven out, thus fulfilling what is stated, Man tarrieth not overnight in his glory. Which Psalm did Adam recite on the first day? The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein; because He created the world, assigned it to mankind, and is the sole Judge of the world. Which did he recite on the second day? Great is the Lord, and highly to be praised, in the city of our God, His holy mountain; because He divided the work of creation and became Sovereign in His universe. Which did he recite on the third day? God standeth in the congregation of God; in the midst of the judges He judgeth; because He then created the sea and the dry land, the earth was rolled into position, and a place was set apart for His people. Which did he recite on the fourth day? O Lord, Thou God to whom vengeance belongeth, Thou God to whom vengeance belongeth, shine forth; because He then created the sun, the moon, the stars and the planets, which give light on earth, and He will in the future punish those who worship them. Which did he recite on the fifth day? Sing aloud unto God our strength; shout unto the God of Jacob; because He then created the birds, the fishes and the sea-monsters, which sing aloud His praises in the world. Which did he recite on the sixth day? The Lord reigneth; He is clothed in majesty; the Lord is clothed, He hath girded Himself with strength; yea the world is established, that it cannot be moved; because He then completed all His works, was exalted and sat enthroned in the heights of the universe. Which did he recite on the seventh day? A Psalm, a Song. For the Sabbath day; because of the day which will be all Sabbath, when there will be neither eating nor drinking nor worldly affairs, but the righteous will sit with crowns on their heads enjoying the brilliance of the Divine Presence, as it is stated, And they beheld God, and did eat and drink, like the ministering angels. And why was this so? In order that [Adam] might immediately partake of the Sabbath meal. R. Simeon b. Eleazar said: I will expound this to you with a parable. To what might Adam be compared? To a man who married a proselyte and used to give her instruction, saying, ‘My dear, do not eat bread when your hands are defiled, do not eat untithed produce, do not profane the Sabbath, do not make vows rashly, and do not associate with another man. If you break one of these rules, you will die’. Now what did a certain man do? He arose and ate in her presence bread although his hands were defiled, he ate before her untithed produce—he profaned the Sabbath and made vows rashly—and also offered her some [of the food]. What could that proselyte have thought to herself? All that my husband forbade me in the beginning was without foundation. She thereupon went and transgressed them all. R. Simeon b. Yoḥai said: I, too, will explain this to you by a parable. To what might Adam be compared? To a man who had his wife at home with him. Now what did that man do? He went and brought a cask into which he put an exact number of figs and nuts. He also caught a scorpion, placed it in the mouth of the cask, covered the cask with a tight-fitting lid and put it away in a corner. He then said to his wife, ‘My dear, all that I possess in this house is at your disposal except this cask which you may not touch under any circumstances’. What did this woman do? No sooner had her husband gone off to market than she arose, opened the cask, put her hand in it and was bitten by the scorpion. Immediately she went and flung herself on her bed. When her husband returned from market he asked her what had happened, and she replied, ‘I put my hand in the cask and was bitten by a scorpion, and now I am dying’. He said to her, ‘Did I not tell you in the beginning that everything I had in the house was at your disposal except that cask which you were not to touch under any circumstances?’ He at once became furious with her and drove her out. So it was with Adam, the first man, when the Holy One, blessed be He, charged him, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat; but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it; for in the day thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die. No sooner had Adam eaten of it than he was driven out [of Eden], to fulfil that which is stated, Man tarrieth not overnight in his glory; he is like the beasts that perish. On the same one day he was formed, created, his outline was shaped, he became solid substance, his limbs were articulated, his orifices opened, a soul was infused into him, he stood on his feet, Eve became his mate, he named [all creatures], was brought into the Garden of Eden, given a command, sinned and was driven out, to fulfil that which is stated, Man tarrieth not overnight in his glory. On that same day two went upon the bed and four came down. R. Judah b. Bathyra said: On that day two went upon the bed and six came down. On that day three decrees were pronounced upon Adam, as it is stated, And unto Adam He said: Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife … cursed is the ground for thy sake; in toil shalt thou eat of it … thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field. When Adam heard that the Holy One, blessed be He, had decreed against him, Thou shalt eat the grass of the field, his limbs forthwith began to tremble and he exclaimed, ‘Lord of the universe! Am I and my beast to eat from one manger?’ Whereupon the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, ‘Since your limbs trembled [at the prospect]’ In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread. Just as three decrees were pronounced upon Adam so were three decrees pronounced upon Eve, as it is stated, I will greatly multiply thy pain and thy travail; in pain thou shalt bring forth children. [I will greatly multiply]—for when a woman begins to experience her monthly flow she suffers pain; I will greatly multiply [thy pain]—for when a woman experiences intercourse for the first time it is painful to her; thy pain [and thy travail]—for during the first three months of pregnancy a woman’s features become coarsened and pallid. As [his first] evening set in and Adam saw the world darkening in the west, he exclaimed, ‘Woe is me! Because I have sinned, the Holy One, blessed be He, is darkening the world upon me!’ He was unaware that such was the course of nature; but in the morning when he saw the world becoming light in the east he was exceedingly happy. He arose and built an altar, he took a bullock whose horns came into being before its hoofs and offered it as a burnt-offering, as it is stated, And it shall please the Lord better than a bullock that hath horns and hoofs. The bullock which Adam offered, the bull which Noah offered, and the ram which our father Abraham offered on the altar instead of his son, were all beasts whose horns came into being before their hoofs, as it is stated, [18a] And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught. Then and there three bands of ministering angels came down with harps and lyres and other musical instruments in their hands and joined with him in a song of praise, as it is stated, A Psalm, a Song. For the Sabbath day. It is a good thing to give thanks unto the Lord…. To declare Thy lovingkindness in the morning, and Thy faithfulness in the night seasons. To declare Thy lovingkindness in the morning—this refers to the world to come which is likened to the brightness of the morning, as it is stated, They are new every morning; great is Thy faithfulness. And Thy faithfulness in the night seasons—this refers to this world which is likened to [the darkness of] night, as it is stated, The burden of Dumah. One calleth unto me out of Seir: Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night? At that time the Holy One, blessed be He, said, ‘If I do not inflict punishment upon the serpent I will be destroying the whole world’. He also said, ‘As for man whom I made lord and king over the world, how he has become entangled [in the wiles of the serpent] and eaten of the [forbidden] tree!’ Thereupon He turned His attention to him and cursed him, as it is stated, And the Lord God said unto the serpent, etc. R. Jose said: Had the curse of the serpent been deferred to later, He would in the meantime have destroyed the whole world. When the Holy One, blessed be He, created Adam, the first man, He formed him behind and before, as it is stated, Thou hast formed me behind and before, and laid Thy hand upon me. Ministering angels descended to adore him, whereupon the Holy One, blessed be He, took him up and placed him beneath His wings, as it is stated, And laid Thy hand upon me. Another interpretation of And laid Thy hand upon me: when Adam sinned, the Holy One, blessed be He, removed one [of His hands] from him. From this it may be inferred that when Adam and the Temple were created, they were each created by His two hands. Whence do we know that man was created by His two hands? For it is stated, Thy hands have made me and fashioned me. And whence do we know that the Temple was created by His two hands? For it is stated, The sanctuary, O Lord, which Thy hands have established. And it is also said, And He brought them to His holy border, to the mountain which His right hand had gotten; and further it is written, The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.”

Then the serpent came and, seeing him in all his glory, at once grew envious of him. How was Adam, the first man, created? Which Psalm did Adam recite on the first day? The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein; because He created the world, assigned it to mankind, and is the sole Judge of the world. Which did he recite on the second day? Great is the Lord, and highly to be praised, in the city of our God, His holy mountain; because He divided the work of creation and became Sovereign in His universe. Which did he recite on the third day? God standeth in the congregation of God; in the midst of the judges He judgeth; because He then created the sea and the dry land, the earth was rolled into position, and a place was set apart for His people. Which did he recite on the fourth day? Which did he recite on the fifth day? Sing aloud unto God our strength; shout unto the God of Jacob; because He then created the birds, the fishes and the sea-monsters, which sing aloud His praises in the world. Which did he recite on the sixth day? Which did he recite on the seventh day? A Psalm, a Song. For the Sabbath day; because of the day which will be all Sabbath, when there will be neither eating nor drinking nor worldly affairs, but the righteous will sit with crowns on their heads enjoying the brilliance of the Divine Presence, as it is stated, And they beheld God, and did eat and drink, like the ministering angels. He went and brought a cask into which he put an exact number of figs and nuts. He also caught a scorpion, placed it in the mouth of the cask, covered the cask with a tight-fitting lid and put it away in a corner. h: Noach’s Trial and Adam’s Spiritual Legacy

p: וְהִנֵּה בְּנֹחַ אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (עג סוֹף עַמּוּד א, וְעַיֵּין שָׁם עו רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א):
— Now behold, concerning Noah it is taught in the holy Zohar in this parashah (73a end, and see there 76a beginning):
בָּעָא נֹחַ לְמִבְדַּק בְּהַהוּא חוֹבָא דִּבְדַק אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— Noah sought to examine that very sin which Adam the First had probed,
לָא לְאִתְדַּבְּקָא בֵּיהּ,
— not to cleave to it,
אֶלָּא לְמִנְדַּע וּלְאַתְקָנָא עָלְמָא וְכוּלֵי,
— rather to know and to rectify the world, etc.,
שֶׁרָצָה לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם וְקִלְקוּל שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן;
— in that he desired to rectify the blemish and corruption of Adam the First;
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נֹחַ אִישׁ צַדִּיק תָּמִים".
— and this is what is stated: ‘Noah was a man, righteous, wholehearted’.
"אִישׁ" מָצִינוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נד:):
— ‘Man’ (ish) we find (Berakhot 54b):
עָמְדוּ עַל גַּבֵּי אִישׁ – זֶה מֹשֶׁה,
— they stood over a man—this is Moses,
דִּכְתִיב: "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו מְאֹד";
— as it is written: ‘Now the man Moses was exceedingly humble’;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּמְּכִילְתָּא (יִתְרוֹ):
— and so they stated in the Mekhilta (Yitro):
כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר "וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ",
— when Scripture states ‘and they asked each man of his fellow’,
מִי קָרוּי אִישׁ? הֲלֹא מֹשֶׁה,
— who is called 'man'? None other than Moses,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה";
— as it is said: ‘Now the man Moses’;
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ (סוֹטָה יד.):
— and so was expounded (Sotah 14a):
"וְלֹא יָדַע אִישׁ" – עַל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, "אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים";
— ‘and no man knew’ refers to Moses our teacher, ‘the man of God’;
וּבְכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי דָּרְשׁוּ "אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים"
— and in several places they expounded ‘the man of God’—
וּבְכַמָּה דּוּכְתֵּי דָּרְשׁוּ "אִישׁ" עַל מֹשֶׁה
— and in several places they expounded 'ish' as referring to Moses
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
— in Midrash Rabbah and the holy Zohar.
"צַדִּיק" – מִדַּת יוֹסֵף,
— ‘Righteous’ (tzaddik)—the attribute of Joseph,
שֶׁהָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם.
— who was the Chariot for the attribute of the Righteous One, Foundation of the World.
"תָּמִים" – שָׁלֵם, מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב "אִישׁ תָּם",
— ‘Wholehearted’ (tamim)—complete, the attribute of Jacob, ‘a simple/wholesome man’ (ish tam),
וּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן: "גְּבַר שְׁלִים".
— which we translate in the Targum: ‘a complete man’.
וּשְׁלָשְׁתָּן קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת:
— And all three embody the sanctity of Shabbat:
דִּבְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא):
— for regarding Jacob our father, peace be upon him, it is taught (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 11):
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי;
— ‘yet Jacob, concerning whom Shabbat observance is written, etc.’;
דְּאַף דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן קִיֵּים מִצְוַת שַׁבָּת,
— for even though Abraham our father likewise fulfilled the mitzvah of Shabbat,
שֶׁהֲרֵי קִיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יוֹמָא כח:),
— seeing that he fulfilled the entire Torah as stated (Yoma 28b),
וּלְגִרְסַת הָרַשְׁבָּ״א בִּתְשׁוּבוֹת וּבְסֵפֶר הָאֶשְׁכּוֹל דְּגָרְסֵי "עֵירוּבֵי תְּחוּמִין"
— and according to the reading of the Rashba in his Responsa and in Sefer HaEshkol who read 'eiruvei techumin'
מְפוֹרָשׁ שֶׁשָּׁמַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
— it is explicit that he observed Shabbat,
וְאַף לְגִרְסָתֵנוּ "עֵירוּבֵי תַּבְשִׁילִין" גַּם כֵּן הַטַּעַם כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּבְרוֹר מָנָה יָפָה לְשַׁבָּת
— and even according to our reading of 'eiruv tavshilin' the rationale is likewise so that he select a choice portion for Shabbat
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בֵּיצָה טו:),
— as stated (Beitzah 15b),
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ: אַבְרָהָם שֶׁאֵין כָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת,
— nonetheless they said: Abraham, in whom Shabbat observance is not written,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִכְתַּב בּוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה בִּפְרָט שֶׁשָּׁמַר שַׁבָּת;
— meaning that it was not written regarding him in the Torah specifically that he kept Shabbat;
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ בִּפְרָט שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת: "וַיִּחַן וְגוֹמֵר",
— whereas regarding Jacob, in whom Shabbat observance is written specifically: ‘and he encamped, etc.’,
זֶה מוֹרֶה שֶׁנִּקְבַּע בּוֹ קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת.
— this demonstrates that the sanctity of Shabbat was permanently established within him.
וְיוֹסֵף גַּם כֵּן מָצִינוּ שֶׁעָשָׂה סְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת,
— And regarding Joseph we likewise find that he prepared a Sabbath feast,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה צב):
— as expounded (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 92):
"וְאֵין 'וְהָכֵן' אֶלָּא שַׁבָּת, הֵיךְ מָה דְּאַתְּ אָמַר: 'וְהָיָה בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי וְהֵכִינוּ'".
— ‘and "prepare" means nothing other than Shabbat, as you say: "And it shall come to pass on the sixth day that they shall prepare"’.
וְכֵן כְּשֶׁחָשַׁב (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תּוֹלְדוֹת) שִׁבְעַת מוּסְפֵי הַמּוֹעֲדִים נֶגֶד שִׁבְעָה רוֹעִים,
— And so when the Zohar Chadash (Toldot) counted the seven Musaf offerings of the festivals corresponding to the seven Shepherds,
חָשַׁב מוּסַף שַׁבָּת נֶגֶד יוֹסֵף,
— he counted the Musaf offering of Shabbat corresponding to Joseph,
שֶׁתּוֹסֶפֶת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁל שַׁבָּת מִבְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף.
— for the additional holiness of Shabbat derives from the dimension of Joseph.
וּמֹשֶׁה גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת,
— And Moses likewise embodies the sanctity of Shabbat,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "יִשְׂמַח מֹשֶׁה בְּמַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ", שֶׁהוּא הַשַּׁבָּת;
— as is said: ‘Moses rejoiced in the gift of his portion’, which is Shabbat;
שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה בֵּירֵר יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִצְרַיִם,
— for Moses selected and instituted the Sabbath day for Israel in Egypt,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שְׁמוֹת א, כח);
— as stated (Midrash Rabbah, Shemot 1:28);
וְאִיתָא בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (תִּיקּוּן יג):
— and it is taught in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 13):
וְהָא מֹשֶׁה תַּמָּן הֲוָה, אֶלָּא מִסִּטְרָא דִּלְגָאו הֲוָה,
— behold Moses was there, but he was from the interior aspect;
דָּא מִגּוּפָא וְדָא מִנִּשְׁמָתָא;
— this one (Jacob) from the body and that one (Moses) from the soul;
שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם גּוּפָא,
— in that Jacob our father, peace be upon him, is the body,
וּמִמֶּנּוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף שֶׁל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ.
— and from him issues the bodily sanctity of all Israel who descended from him.
וְיַעֲקֹב וְיוֹסֵף כַּחֲדָא אִינּוּן,
— And Jacob and Joseph are as one,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, קעו סוֹף עַמּוּד ב);
— as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 176b end);
וְנֶפֶשׁ הַדָּם הוּא חַיּוּת הַגּוּף,
— and the soul of the blood is the vitality of the body,
וְיוֹסֵף נִקְרָא "חַי עָלְמִין" כַּיָּדוּעַ,
— and Joseph is called 'the Life of the Worlds' as is known,
וּבְחִינָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא חַיּוּת הַגּוּף וְהוּא נֶגֶד הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
— and his dimension is the vitality of the body corresponding to the nefesh,
וּמְבָרֵר נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם בִּקְדוּשָׁה.
— and he refines the souls (nefashot) of Israel that they be in holiness.
וּמֹשֶׁה נִשְׁמָתָא,
— And Moses is the neshamah,
שֶׁהוּא קְדוּשַּׁת שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
— which is the holy root of the souls of Israel
שֶׁהֵם מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
— which stem from the words of Torah,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם".
— as is stated: ‘The spirit of man is the lamp of Hashem’.
וְכָל נְשָׁמָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה,
— And every single Jewish soul has a root in the Torah,
אוֹת אוֹ חֵלֶק מֵאוֹת,
— a letter or a fragment of a letter,
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת "תּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה".
— and Moses our teacher is the root of all words of Torah, which is called 'the Torah of Moses'.
וּשְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלּוּ בָּאוּ לְתַקֵּן פְּגָם שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּגוּף, וְנֶפֶשׁ, וּנְשָׁמָה.
— And these three came to rectify the blemish of Adam the First in body, nefesh, and neshamah.
וְנֹחַ שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ "אִישׁ צַדִּיק תָּמִים",
— And Noah, concerning whom it is written 'a man, righteous, wholehearted',
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב, יוֹסֵף וּמֹשֶׁה כָּאָמוּר,
— which alludes to the aspects of Jacob, Joseph, and Moses as explained,
בָּעָא גַּם כֵּן לְתַקָּנָא עָלְמָא מִפְּגָם אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— sought likewise to rectify the world from the blemish of Adam the First,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
— and as stated in the holy Zohar.
וְכֵן אִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כה):
— And so it is brought (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 25):
כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָמַד נֹחַ – נָחוּ,
— as soon as Noah arose, they rested;
וּמִנַּיִן לָנוּ?
— and whence do we know this?
נֶאֱמַר כָּאן נִיחָא,
— It is stated here an expression of resting,
וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן: "לְמַעַן יָנוּחַ וְגוֹמֵר",
— and stated elsewhere: ‘that your ox may rest, etc.’,
מְרַמֵּז שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן מֵעֵין נִיחָא דְּשַׁבָּת,
— alluding that within him was likewise a semblance of Sabbath rest,
שֶׁהָיָה "אִישׁ צַדִּיק תָּמִים" בְּחִינַת שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלּוּ,
— for he was 'a man, righteous, wholehearted,' embodying these three dimensions,
שֶׁהֵם יַעֲקֹב, יוֹסֵף וּמֹשֶׁה.
— which are Jacob, Joseph, and Moses.
וְעַל כֵּן רָצָה גַּם כֵּן לְתַקֵּן פְּגָם אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— Therefore he also desired to rectify the blemish of Adam the First,
אַךְ "וְלָא יָכִיל", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ;
— yet 'he was not able', as stated in the holy Zohar;
שֶׁאַף שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ שְׁלֹשׁ בְּחִינוֹת אֵלּוּ,
— for even though he possessed these three dimensions,
הָיָה רַק "בְּדֹרֹתָיו",
— it was only 'in his generations',
שֶׁבְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה לֹא הָיָה נֶחְשָׁב לִכְלוּם נֶגֶד מֹשֶׁה,
— for in the generation of Moses he would have been considered as nothing relative to Moses,
וְכֵן לֹא הָיָה נֶחְשָׁב לִכְלוּם נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב וְיוֹסֵף,
— and likewise he would have been considered as nothing relative to Jacob and Joseph,
שֶׁאַדְּרַבָּה, לוֹ נֶאֱמַר: "וְיוֹם וָלַיְלָה לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ";
— for on the contrary, unto him it was said: ‘and day and night they shall not cease’;
וְזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת פְּתִיחָה זוֹ לְפָרָשַׁת נֹחַ:
— and this is the connection of this opening discourse to Parashat Noach.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 54b:3: “It is taught in the midrash: They are the stones that remained suspended in the air and did not fall because of [al gav] a man [ish] and they fell down because of [al gav] a man [ish]. The Gemara explains: They remained suspended because of a man; that is Moses, whom the verse refers to as a man, as it is written: “And the man Moses was very modest” (Numbers 12:3), and it is written: “And Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh, and spread forth his hands unto the Lord; the thunders and hail ceased, and the rain was not poured upon the earth” (Exodus 9:33). Moses’ hailstones remained suspended. And the stones descended because of a man; that is Joshua, who was also called man, as it is written: “Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is spirit” (Numbers 27:18). And it is written that when Joshua and his people waged war against the army of the Emorite kings, God told him not to fear them because God would deliver them into his hands; and indeed, they died by means of these stones: “As they fled from before Israel, while they were at the descent of Beit Ḥoron, that the Lord cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto Azeka, and they died; they were more who died with the hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew by sword” (Joshua 10:11).”

paragraphs.text: Sotah 14a: ‘Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: Even Moses our teacher himself does not know where he is buried. It is written here: “And no man knows of his grave,” and it is written there: “And this is the blessing wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death” (Deuteronomy 33:1). In other words, even Moses, as he is referred to by the term “man,” does not know his burial place. And Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: For what reason was Moses buried near Beth Peor? In order to atone for the incident that transpired at Beth Peor (Numbers, chapter 25).’

paragraphs.text: Yoma 28b:9: “Apropos the previous statement, the Gemara cites that Rav said: Abraham our Patriarch fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given, as it is stated: “Because [ekev] Abraham hearkened to My voice and kept My charge, My mitzvot, My statutes and My Torahs” (Genesis 26:5). Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya said to Rav: And say that the verse means that he fulfilled only the seven Noahide mitzvot and not the entire Torah. The Gemara asks: But isn’t there also circumcision that Abraham clearly observed, which is not one of the Noahide laws? Apparently, Abraham fulfilled more than just those seven. The Gemara asks: And say that he fulfilled only the seven mitzvot and circumcision. Rav said to him: If so, why do I need the continuation of the verse, that Abraham kept: My mitzvot and My Torah? That is a clear indication that he fulfilled mitzvot beyond the seven Noahide mitzvot, and apparently fulfilled the entire Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Beitzah 15b:7: “We learned in the mishna: One may prepare a cooked dish on a Festival eve and rely on it to cook for Shabbat. Granted, according to Rav Ashi, who said that the reason for an eiruv is so that people will say: One may not bake on a Festival for Shabbat; that is why on a Festival eve, yes, one may prepare the eiruv, but on the Festival itself, no, one may not do so, as it is a reminder that in principle one may not cook on a Festival for Shabbat. However, according to Rava, who stated that the reason for the eiruv is to ensure that one selects choice portions for both the Festival and Shabbat, why does the mishna discuss specifically preparation on a Festival eve? Even were one to prepare a dish for Shabbat on the Festival as well, it would guarantee that he accord the appropriate deference to Shabbat.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 25:2: ““He called his name Noah, saying: This one will comfort us from our work and from the misery of our hands, from the ground, which the Lord cursed” (Genesis 5:29). “He called his name Noah, saying,” Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The interpretation does not correspond to the name and the name does not correspond to the interpretation. It should have said instead: ‘Noah, this one will give us rest [yaniḥenu],’ or ‘Naḥman, this one will comfort us [yenaḥamenu].’ However, when the Holy One blessed be He created Adam the first man, He gave him control over everything; the cow would heed the plowman and [even] the furrow would heed the plowman. When Adam sinned, they rebelled against him; the cow did not heed the plowman and the furrow did not heed the plowman. When Noah appeared, they abstained [naḥu]. From where is that derived? Rest [neyaḥa] is stated here and elsewhere it is stated: “So that your ox and your donkey will rest [yanuaḥ]” (Exodus 23:12). Just as neyaḥa that is stated there refers to the resting of an ox, so, too, neyaḥa that is stated here refers to the resting of an ox. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: The name does not correspond with the interpretation and interpretation does not correspond with the name. It should have said instead: ‘Noah, this one will give us rest [yaniḥenu],’ or ‘Naḥman, this one will comfort us [yenaḥamenu].’ However, until Noah appeared, the water would rise and inundate them in their graves. “Who calls the water of the sea” is written twice (Amos 5:8; 9:6) corresponding to the two times that the water would rise and inundate them in their graves, once in the morning and once in the evening. That is what is written: “Like corpses lying in the grave” (Psalms 88:6) – those of them who were lying were desecrated. When Noah appeared, they rested [in their graves]. Rest [neyaḥa] is stated here and elsewhere it is stated: “May he depart in peace…may they rest [yanuḥu] upon their resting places” (Isaiah 57:2). Just as neyaḥa that is stated there refers to the rest of the grave, so, too, neyaḥa that is stated here refers to the rest of the grave. Rabbi Eliezer said: He was called after the name of his offering, as it is stated: “The Lord smelled the pleasing [niḥoaḥ] aroma” (Genesis 8:21). Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Ḥanina said: He was called for the name of the resting of the ark, as it is written: “The ark rested [vatanaḥ]” (Genesis 8:4). Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The constellations did not function all those twelve months [of the Flood]. Rabbi Yonatan said to him: They functioned, but their effect was imperceptible. “[All the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, night and day] will not cease” (Genesis 8:22), Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Eliezer said: “Will not cease” – from here we learn that they did not cease [during the Flood]. Rabbi Eliezer said: “Will not cease” – [on the contrary,] from here we learn that they did cease.”

Rest [neyaḥa] is stated here and elsewhere it is stated: “So that your ox and your donkey will rest [yanuaḥ]” (Exodus 23:12). Just as neyaḥa that is stated there refers to the resting of an ox, so, too, neyaḥa that is stated here refers to the resting of an ox. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: The name does not correspond with the interpretation and interpretation does not correspond with the name. It should have said instead: ‘Noah, this one will give us rest [yaniḥenu],’ or ‘Naḥman, this one will comfort us [yenaḥamenu].’ However, until Noah appeared, the water would rise and inundate them in their graves. “Who calls the water of the sea” is written twice (Amos 5:8; 9:6) corresponding to the two times that the water would rise and inundate them in their graves, once in the morning and once in the evening. That is what is written: “Like corpses lying in the grave” (Psalms 88:6) – those of them who were lying were desecrated. When Noah appeared, they rested [in their graves]. Rest [neyaḥa] is stated here and elsewhere it is stated: “May he depart in peace…may they rest [yanuḥu] upon their resting places” (Isaiah 57:2). Just as neyaḥa that is stated there refers to the rest of the grave, so, too, neyaḥa that is stated here refers to the rest of the grave. Rabbi Eliezer said: He was called after the name of his offering, as it is stated: “The Lord smelled the pleasing [niḥoaḥ] aroma” (Genesis 8:21). Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Ḥanina said: He was called for the name of the resting of the ark, as it is written: “The ark rested [vatanaḥ]” (Genesis 8:4). Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The constellations did not function all those twelve months [of the Flood]. Rabbi Yonatan said to him: They functioned, but their effect was imperceptible. “[All the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, night and day] will not cease” (Genesis 8:22), Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Eliezer said: “Will not cease” – from here we learn that they did not cease [during the Flood]. Rabbi Eliezer said: “Will not cease” – [on the contrary,] from here we learn that they did cease.”

h: Noach Walked with God: His Spiritual Stature

p: וּבַזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (כב עַמּוּד ב):
— And in Zohar Chadash in this parashah (22b):
"'אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים הִתְהַלֶּךְ נֹחַ'
— ‘"Noah walked with God"—
לְמַעְלָה עַל כָּל הַמַּעֲלוֹת.
— above all spiritual levels.
'וַיּוֹלֶד נֹחַ שְׁלֹשָׁה בָנִים'
— "And Noah begot three sons"—
תָּאנֵי רַבִּי כְּרוּסְפְּדַאי:
— Rabbi Kruspedai taught:
אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה הַנְהָגוֹת אֲשֶׁר בָּאָדָם:
— these are three modes of conduct within man:
הַנְהָגַת הַנְּשָׁמָה לִהְיוֹת לוֹ עֵזֶר בַּעֲבוֹדַת בּוֹרְאוֹ,
— the guidance of the neshamah to serve as an aid in the service of his Creator,
וְהִיא הַנִּקְרֵאת שֵׁם;
— and this is called Shem;
וְהַנְהָגַת הַתַּאֲוָה וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הַמַּנְהִיג וּמְחַמֵּם אֶת הַגּוּף,
— and the conduct of lust and the evil inclination that drives and heats the body,
וְהִיא הַנִּקְרֵאת חָם;
— and this is called Ham;
וְהַנְהָגַת הַיֵּצֶר טוֹב וְכוּלֵי
— and the conduct of the good inclination, etc.,
וּלְיַפּוֹת מַעֲשָׂיו בַּתּוֹרָה וּבְיִרְאַת ה',
— and to beautify his deeds in Torah and fear of Hashem,
וְהִיא הַנִּקְרֵאת יֶפֶת וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— and this is called Japheth, etc.’, see there.
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים דִּכְתִיב "אִישׁ צַדִּיק תָּמִים",
— And this likewise corresponds to the three designations written: 'a man, righteous, wholehearted',
שֶׁהֵם קְדוּשַּׁת מֹשֶׁה, יַעֲקֹב וְיוֹסֵף כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
— which are the sanctities of Moses, Jacob, and Joseph, as we said.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁ"הִתְהַלֶּךְ אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים" לְמַעְלָה עַל כָּל הַמַּעֲלוֹת,
— Namely, through his 'walking with God' above all levels,
זָכָה לִשְׁלֹשׁ בְּחִינוֹת אֵלּוּ:
— he merited these three dimensions:
הַנְהָגַת הַנְּשָׁמָה;
— the conduct of the neshamah;
וְלִכְבּוֹשׁ אֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וּלְכוֹבְשׁוֹ,
— and to subdue the evil inclination and conquer it,
שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" – בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ, בְּיֵצֶר טוֹב וּבְיֵצֶר רָע,
— concerning which it is said: ‘with all your heart’—with both your inclinations, the good and the evil,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (בְּרָכוֹת נד.);
— as stated at the start of chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 54a);
וּלְהַנְהָגַת הַיֵּצֶר טוֹב.
— and the conduct of the good inclination.
וַחֲשָׁבָם כְּסֵדֶר הַבְּרִיאָה:
— And he enumerated them in the order of development:
שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה נִיתְּנָה בָּאָדָם מִשְּׁעַת פְּקִידָה,
— for the neshamah is placed in man from the moment of conception,
וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שׁוֹלֵט בָּאָדָם מִשְּׁעַת יְצִיאָה,
— and the evil inclination rules over man from the moment of birth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (סַנְהֶדְרִין צא:);
— as stated (Sanhedrin 91b);
וְהַיֵּצֶר טוֹב בָּא לָאָדָם מִשֶּׁנַּעֲשָׂה בֶּן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה,
— and the good inclination enters a person once he reaches thirteen years of age,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב קעט עַמּוּד א).
— as stated in the holy Zohar (start of Parashat Vayeishev 179a).
וְחָשַׁב הַנְהָגַת הַנְּשָׁמָה נֶגֶד קְדוּשַׁת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ,
— And he counted the conduct of the neshamah corresponding to the holiness of Moses our teacher,
דְּאִיהוּ נִשְׁמָתָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּתִּיקּוּנִים,
— for he is the neshamah, as stated in the Tikkunim,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
— being the root of all words of Torah
שֶׁמִּשָּׁם שׁוֹרֶשׁ נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— whence is the root of the souls of Israel,
וְנִקְרָא "אִישׁ".
— and he is called 'man' (ish).
וְחָם כְּנֶגֶד הַנְהָגַת הַתַּאֲוָה,
— And Ham corresponds to the conduct of bodily desire,
וְהַיְינוּ לִהְיוֹת גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ,
— namely to be a hero who conquers his inclination,
וְזֶהוּ כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַׁת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק.
— and this corresponds to the holiness of Joseph who was the Chariot for the attribute of Tzaddik.
וְיֶפֶת כְּנֶגֶד יֵצֶר טוֹב,
— And Japheth corresponds to the good inclination,
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁנִּקְרָא "אִישׁ תָּם"
— and corresponds to the aspect of Jacob who is called 'a wholehearted man'
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ כְּלָל יֵצֶר הָרָע,
— who possessed no evil inclination at all,
שֶׁהָיָה כְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל
— for he was like Adam the First prior to the fall,
וְלֹא יָדַע כְּלָל מֵעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ
— and knew nothing at all of the counsel of the Serpent,
שֶׁהוּא הַהַרְגָּשׁ בַּהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ;
— which is the self-centered experience of one's own pleasure, as explained;
וְזֶה הַנְהָגַת הַיֵּצֶר טוֹב כְּצַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים
— and this is the conduct of the good inclination like completely righteous ones
שֶׁרַק יֵצֶר טוֹב שׁוֹפְטָן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּרָכוֹת סא:),
— whom only the good inclination judges (as stated in Berakhot 61b),
וְלֹא כִּקְדוּשַׁת יוֹסֵף בְּחִינַת צַדִּיק,
— and not like the holiness of Joseph in the aspect of Tzaddik,
שֶׁהוּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ יֵצֶר הָרָע
— which consists of the presence of an evil inclination
וְהַצַּדִּיק מִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה וְכוֹבְשׁוֹ.
— and the righteous one overpowers his inclination through awe and subdues it.
רַק שֶׁכָּל הַקְּדוּשׁוֹת הָיָה לוֹ רַק בְּדוֹרוֹתָיו,
— Only that all these sanctities Noah possessed solely in his generations,
וְלֹא זָכָה לָהֶם כְּמוֹ מֹשֶׁה, יוֹסֵף וְיַעֲקֹב
— and did not merit them on the supreme level of Moses, Joseph, and Jacob,
שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ:
— who are the foundational root of the holiness of Shabbat, as we explained.

h: The Sweet Fragrance After the Flood

p: וְאִיתָא אַחַר כָּךְ בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (כג עַמּוּד א):
— And it is brought afterward in Zohar Chadash (23a):
רַבִּי פָּתַח: "'וַיָּרַח ה' אֶת רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ' וְגוֹמֵר,
— Rabbi opened: ‘"And Hashem smelled the sweet savor, etc.";
כְּשֶׁיָּצָא נֹחַ וְכוּלֵי
— when Noah went forth, etc.,
הִתְחִיל בּוֹכֶה עַל הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי
— he began weeping over the world, etc.,
וְקָם וְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְפָנָיו,
— and arose and prayed before Him,
וְאוֹתוֹ הָרֵיחַ עָלָה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְעָרַב לוֹ.
— and that fragrance ascended before the Holy One, blessed be He, and was pleasing to Him.
אָמַר רַבִּי: שְׁלֹשָׁה רֵיחוֹת עָלוּ לְפָנָיו:
— Rabbi said: Three fragrances ascended before Him:
רֵיחַ עוֹלָתוֹ, וְרֵיחַ תְּפִלָּתוֹ, וְרֵיחַ מַעֲשָׂיו;
— the fragrance of his burnt-offering, the fragrance of his prayer, and the fragrance of his deeds;
וְלֹא הָיָה רֵיחַ בָּעוֹלָם דְּנִיחָא קַמֵּיהּ כְּאוֹתוֹ הָרֵיחַ,
— and there was no fragrance in the world so pleasing before Him as that fragrance,
וּלְפִיכָךְ צִוָּה וְאָמַר: 'רֵיחַ נִיחֹחִי תִּשְׁמְרוּ לְהַקְרִיב לִי',
— and therefore He commanded and said: "My sweet savor shall you observe to offer unto Me"—
כְּלוֹמַר: רֵיחַ שֶׁהִקְרִיב נֹחַ לְפָנַי תִּשְׁמְרוּ לְהַקְרִיב לִי:
— meaning: the fragrance that Noah offered before Me shall you observe to offer unto Me:
רֵיחַ עוֹלָה, וּתְפִלָּה, וְכִשְׁרוֹן מַעֲשִׂים".
— the fragrance of burnt-offering, prayer, and virtuous deeds.’
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכְּשֶׁיָּצָא נֹחַ וְרָאָה חוּרְבַּן הָעוֹלָם
— Namely, when Noah went forth and saw the destruction of the world,
בָּכָה עֲלֵיהֶם וְהִתְפַּלֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם,
— he wept over them and prayed for them,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְהַלָּן שָׁם בַּאֲרִיכוּת;
— as is stated further on there at length;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֱשִׁיבוֹ:
— and Hashem answered him:
כְּעַן אָמְרַת דָּא
— ‘Only now do you say this,
וְלָא בְּזִמְנָא דַּאֲמָרִית לָךְ בְּלִישָׁנָא רַכִּיכָא
— and not at the time I spoke to you in gentle language,
דִּכְתִיב: 'כִּי אֹתְךָ רָאִיתִי וְגוֹמֵר',
— where it is written: "For you have I seen, etc.",
בְּדִיל דְּתִבְעֵי רַחֲמִין עַל עָלְמָא וְכוּלֵי.
— in order that you plead for mercy upon the world, etc.?’
וְאִם הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל אָז הָיָה מְבַטֵּל הַגְּזֵירָה,
— And had he prayed then, he would have annulled the decree,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, סז עַמּוּד ב);
— as written there and in the holy Zohar (Part I, 67b);
וְכֵיוָן דַּחֲזָא נֹחַ כָּךְ,
— and once Noah saw this,
הִקְרִיב עִלָּוָון וְקָרְבָּנִין וְכוּלֵי.
— he offered burnt-offerings and sacrifices, etc.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "שְׁלֹשָׁה רֵיחוֹת עָלוּ לְפָנָיו",
— And this is what it meant: ‘three fragrances ascended before Him’,
שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן כְּנֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשׁוֹת בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה, יַעֲקֹב וְיוֹסֵף
— which likewise correspond to the three sanctities of Moses, Jacob, and Joseph
שֶׁנִּרְמַז בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "אִישׁ צַדִּיק תָּמִים",
— alluded to in the verse 'a man, righteous, wholehearted',
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת:
— and as we said, they are the root of the holiness of Shabbat:
רֵיחַ עוֹלָתוֹ כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַׁת יוֹסֵף
— The fragrance of his burnt-offering corresponds to the holiness of Joseph,
שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ מוּסַף שַׁבָּת,
— counter to whom stands the Musaf offering of Shabbat,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ תּוֹלְדוֹת.
— as stated in Zohar Chadash, Toldot.
וְרֵיחַ תְּפִלָּתוֹ נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
— And the fragrance of his prayer corresponds to the holiness of Moses our teacher,
שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל דּוֹרוֹ וּמָסַר נַפְשׁוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם,
— who prayed for his generation and gave his soul for them,
וְלֹא כְּנֹחַ, שֶׁאַף שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל אַחַר כָּךְ הָיָה שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנּוֹ;
— unlike Noah, whose subsequent prayer was not in its proper time;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם עָרַב לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹתוֹ הָרֵיחַ,
— nonetheless that fragrance was pleasing to Hashem,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ.
— as stated in Zohar Chadash.
וְרֵיחַ מַעֲשָׂיו כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
— And the fragrance of his deeds corresponds to the holiness of Jacob our father, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא גּוּפָא,
— who is the body,
וּמִמֶּנּוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף שֶׁל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם זַרְעוֹ,
— and from him derives the sanctity of the body of all Israel who are his seed,
וְהַמַּעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים הֵם בַּגּוּף.
— and good deeds are executed in the body.
וְאָז עָלָה הָרֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ
— And then the sweet fragrance ascended,
שֶׁהָיָה כָּלוּל בּוֹ מֵעֵין שָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשׁוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרוֹת.
— which encompassed a semblance of these three aforementioned sanctities.
וְהֵם כּוּלָּם שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁהִיא מִדַּת מַלְכוּת.
— And all of them are the root of the holiness of Shabbat, which is the attribute of Malchut.

h: The Offering Made for the Sake of Heaven

p: רֵיחַ עוֹלָתוֹ – הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת,
— The fragrance of his burnt-offering—the sacrifices,
"לְרֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ" – לְשֵׁם הַנָּחַת רוּחַ,
— ‘for a sweet savor’—for the sake of divine satisfaction,
לְשֵׁם מִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם,
— for the sake of He Who spoke and the world came into being,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (זְבָחִים מו:);
— as stated (Zevachim 46b);
וְכָל עִיקַּר הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ,
— and the primary purpose of Creation is that the glory of His sovereignty be revealed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (סוֹף פֶּרֶק ו דְּאָבוֹת מִשְׁנָה יא):
— as stated (end of Avot 6:11):
"כָּל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ לֹא בְרָאוֹ אֶלָּא לִכְבוֹדוֹ וְכוּלֵי,
— ‘Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world He created solely for His glory, etc.,
וְלִכְבוֹדִי בְּרָאתִיו";
— and for My glory have I created it’;
וְכֵן אָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק "כָּל פָּעַל ה' לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ"
— and so they expounded on the verse ‘Hashem made everything for His sake’—
"לְקִילּוּסוֹ", שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְקַלְּסִין אוֹתוֹ,
— ‘for His praise’, that they should praise Him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים קמח);
— as stated (Shocher Tov, Tehillim 148);
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר (שַׁבָּת לא:):
— and elsewhere (Shabbat 31b):
"לֹא בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ
— ‘The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world only
אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּירְאוּ מִלְּפָנָיו,
— so that they should fear before Him,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'וְהָאֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה שֶׁיִּרְאוּ מִלְּפָנָיו'".
— as it is said: "And God has made it that men should fear before Him"’.
אֲבָל שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת:
— Yet both are true:
דִּ"לְיִרְאָה" זֶה קָאֵי עַל הָאָדָם
— for 'to fear' refers to man,
שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית מְכֻוָּון הַבְּרִיאָה,
— who is the ultimate intended goal of Creation,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אָנֹכִי עָשִׂיתִי אֶרֶץ וְאָדָם עָלֶיהָ בָרָאתִי";
— as is stated: ‘I have made the earth, and created man upon it’;
וְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה וְכוּלֵי,
— and the entire world was created solely for the sake of this, etc.,
כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא לְצַוּוֹת לָזֶה
— the entire world was created solely to accompany this one
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּרָכוֹת ו:);
— (as stated in Berakhot 6b);
וְהוּא נִבְרָא לְיִרְאָה,
— and he was created for awe,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה".
— and as is stated: ‘What does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear’.
וּבְרִיאַת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ הוּא לִכְבוֹדוֹ,
— And the creation of the entire universe is for His glory,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָאָדָם יַשִּׂיג מִזֶּה כְּבוֹדוֹ;
— meaning that man should attain from it His glory;
וְזֶה הָאוֹר שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן
— and this is the primordial light created on the first day,
שֶׁהָיָה הָאָדָם צוֹפֶה וּמַבִּיט בּוֹ מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ,
— wherein man could gaze and see from one end of the world to the other,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (חֲגִיגָה יב.),
— as stated (Chagigah 12a),
הַיְינוּ לְהַכִּיר מִכָּל הַבְּרִיאָה כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ.
— meaning to recognize from all of Creation the glory of His kingship.
וְהַיְינוּ שַׁבָּת: דְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת אִיהִי יִרְאָה וְשַׁרְיָא בָּהּ יִרְאָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, ה עַמּוּד ב),
— And this is Shabbat: for Shabbat eve is awe, and awe rests within it (Zohar Part I, 5b),
מֶלֶךְ שֶׁתְּהֵא אֵימָתוֹ עָלֶיךָ.
— a king, whose dread should be upon you.
וּמִזֶּה גַּם כֵּן רֵיחַ תְּפִלָּה שֶׁבָּא מִמִּדָּה זוֹ,
— And from this likewise derives the fragrance of prayer which stems from this attribute,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח",
— and as is stated: ‘O Lord (Adonai), open my lips’,
וְשֵׁם זֶה מוֹרֶה עַל יִרְאָה,
— and this Name denotes awe,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאִם אֲדוֹנִים אָנִי אַיֵּה מוֹרָאִי".
— as is stated: ‘And if I be a Master, where is My fear?’
וּבַגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת ט:) נִדְרַשׁ: "יִירָאוּךָ עִם שָׁמֶשׁ" – עַל תְּפִלָּה;
— And in the Gemara (Berakhot 9b) it was expounded: ‘They shall fear You with the sun’—referring to prayer;
וְכֵן (שָׁם י:):
— and likewise (there, 10b):
"אַל יִמְנַע עַצְמוֹ מִן הָרַחֲמִים וְכוּלֵי כִּי אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים יָרֵא",
— ‘Let one not withhold himself from mercy, etc., for he fears God’,
נִדְרַשׁ לְשׁוֹן יִרְאָה עַל תְּפִלָּה וְרַחֲמִים;
— the terminology of fear is expounded regarding prayer and mercy;
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ (שָׁם ו:):
— and so too it was expounded (there, 6b):
"'מִי בָכֶם יְרֵא ה' וְגוֹמֵר'
— ‘"Who among you fears Hashem, etc."—
עַל הָרָגִיל לָבֹא לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— referring to one accustomed to come to the synagogue, etc.’, see there.
וְכֵן רֵיחַ מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים הוּא מִמִּדָּה זוֹ,
— And likewise the fragrance of good deeds is from this attribute,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, קכג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)
— as stated in the holy Zohar (Part III, 123b beginning)
דְּהֵ״א תַּתָּאָה כְּנֶגֶד מִצְוָה.
— that the lower Hei corresponds to mitzvah.
וְכָל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל כְּעוֹשֶׂה מִצְוָה
— And throughout the entire Sabbath day a Jew is considered as performing a mitzvah
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּיצּוֹל מֵעֲבֵירַת חִלּוּל שַׁבָּת,
— by virtue of being saved from the sin of Sabbath desecration,
וּכְמַקְרִיב קָרְבַּן מוּסָף עַל יְדֵי הָאַהֲבָה וְחֵשֶׁק לַעֲשׂוֹת,
— and like one who offers the Musaf sacrifice through love and yearning to perform it,
וְנֶאֱנַס וְלֹא עָשָׂה, שֶׁמַּעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ עֲשָׂאָהּ.
— and was prevented by circumstance, wherein Scripture credits him as though he performed it.
וְהַתְּפִלָּה בְּשַׁבָּת רְצוּיָה,
— And prayer on Shabbat is deeply acceptable,
שֶׁהִיא רַק עַל צָרְכֵי הַנֶּפֶשׁ, עַל מִצְווֹת וְתוֹרָה
— for it is only for the needs of the soul, for mitzvot and Torah
וְטָהֳרַת הַלֵּב לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת
— and purity of heart for the service of Hashem in truth
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ג);
— (and as explained in Discourse 3);
וְזוֹכִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכָל הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה רֵיחוֹת דְּאָמַר,
— and Israel merit all three fragrances concerning which it said

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tehillim 148:1: ““Hallelujah. Praise the Lord from the heavens”: those who are in the heavens. Who are they? The ministering angels. “Praise Him, all His angels.” Just as there are many hosts on earth, so there are in heaven: “These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created” (Genesis 2:4). Therefore it says, “Praise Him, all His hosts.” Who are His hosts? Those who do the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “Bless the Lord, all His hosts” (Psalms 103:21). Therefore it says, “Praise Him, all His hosts.” “Praise Him, sun and moon.” Who are the sun and moon? The patriarchs and matriarchs, who are compared to the sun and moon, as it says, “And behold, the sun and the moon” (Genesis 37:9). “Praise Him, all stars of light.” Who are the stars of light? The righteous, as it says, “Those who lead the many to righteousness are like the stars” (Daniel 12:3). Therefore it says, “Praise Him, all stars of light.” From here you learn that each of them has a star in heaven, and his star shines according to his deeds. Therefore it says: Praise Him, those whose stars shine. “Praise Him, heavens of heavens.” From here you learn that there are only three heavens—the reading given in the name of Radal. So it says, “Behold, the heavens and the heavens of heavens” (I Kings 8:27). Therefore it says, “Praise Him.” These are the waters, those waters of Creation, as it says, “God called the firmament ‘heavens’” (Genesis 1:8): it bears water. “Let them praise the name of the Lord.” The Holy One, blessed be He, had no toil when He created them, as it says, “On the day that the Lord God made” (Genesis 2:4), and it is written, “For in six days the Lord made” (Exodus 20:11). The Holy One, blessed be He, had no toil; He only commanded, and they came into being of themselves. Therefore it says, “Let them praise the name of the Lord,” for they were created on this condition: to praise Him. “He established them forever and ever; He gave a decree that shall not pass.” What decree did He give? He said to them, “Let there be a firmament” (Genesis 1:6). From that day they have not moved. The Holy One, blessed be He, created the world to rejoice in it. Yet, as it were, He had no joy in it, because Adam sinned and the ground was cursed, as it says, “Cursed is the ground” (Genesis 3:17). Cain came and killed Abel. He said to him, “Where is Abel your brother?” (Genesis 4:9), “The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground” (Genesis 4:10), and “You shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth” (Genesis 4:12). He did not let the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoice in His works.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 31b: ‘fear of Heaven is like a treasurer [gizbar] to whom they gave keys to the inner doors of the treasury but they did not give keys to the outer door. With what key will he enter? Although the Torah is the inner key, without fear of Heaven one cannot gain access to the genuine Torah. Similarly, Rabbi Yannai would proclaim: Woe unto one who does not have a courtyard, and who makes a fence for the courtyard, i.e., a person who lacks fear of Heaven and is nevertheless involved in Torah study. Rav Yehuda said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, only created His world so that people would fear before Him, as it is stated: “And God has so made it that men should fear before Him” (Ecclesiastes 3:14).’

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 6b: ‘Additionally, Ravin bar Rav Adda said that Rabbi Yitzḥak said: One who is accustomed to come to the synagogue and did not come one day, the Holy One, Blessed be He, asks about him, as it were, to determine what happened to him, as it is stated: “Who among you fears the Lord? Who hears the voice of His servant? Though he walks in darkness and has no light, let him trust in the name of the Lord, and rely upon his God” (Isaiah 50:10). In other words, God asks, who among you fears the Lord yet did not come to hear the voice of His servant the prayer leader, who engages in the service of God? He who went out before dawn and walks in darkness before prayer.’
